Hello,

As a debugging agent, I have analyzed the provided Dockerfile and build error. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Identification

The root cause of the build failure is an outdated URL for downloading the METIS library.

The build log clearly shows the following sequence:
1.  `wget` attempts to download from `http://glaros.dtc.umn.edu/gkhome/fetch/sw/metis/metis-5.1.0.tar.gz`.
2.  The server responds with a `301 Moved Permanently` redirect, pointing `wget` to a new location: `https://karypis.github.io/gkhome/fetch/sw/metis/metis-5.1.0.tar.gz`.
3.  `wget` follows the redirect but receives a `404 Not Found` error from the new URL.

This indicates that the METIS source archive is no longer available at the specified location.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this issue, we must update the URL to point to a valid source for METIS and adjust for the new archive's directory structure. The official source code is now hosted on GitHub.

The fix involves two small changes:
1.  Replace the old `wget` URL with the correct one from the official METIS GitHub repository.
2.  Update the `cd` command to match the directory name (`METIS-5.1.0`) created when extracting the archive from GitHub.

Here is the corrected Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, modern environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during build
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments, especially on cloud platforms like AWS
# This allows MPI to run as root (common in containers) and correctly uses the container's network interface.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0

# A single RUN layer is used to install dependencies, build the application, and clean up.
# This adheres to the constraints of not using multi-stage builds or COPY/ADD commands.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    make \
    cmake \
    && mkdir /build && cd /build \
    \
    # --- Build and install METIS 5.1.0 ---
    # A graph partitioning library required by MFEM.
    # FIX: Switched to the stable, official METIS download URL and corrected the extracted directory path.
    && wget https://github.com/KarypisLab/METIS/archive/refs/tags/v5.1.0.tar.gz -O metis-5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && tar -xzvf metis-5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && cd METIS-5.1.0 \
    && make config shared=1 prefix=/usr/local \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd .. \
    \
    # --- Build and install Hypre ---
    # A library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers required by MFEM.
    && wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre.tar.gz \
    && tar -xzvf hypre.tar.gz \
    && cd hypre-2.28.0/src \
    && ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --disable-fortran --enable-shared \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd ../.. \
    \
    # --- Build and install MFEM (Modular Finite Element Methods library) ---
    # The core finite element discretization library on which Laghos is built.
    && git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make config MFEM_USE_METIS_5=YES MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local METIS_DIR=/usr/local \
    && make parallel -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd .. \
    \
    # Update the dynamic linker's cache to find the newly installed shared libraries
    && ldconfig \
    \
    # --- Build Laghos Application ---
    # Clones the latest version from the default branch and builds the executable.
    && git clone --depth 1 --recursive https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git \
    && cd Laghos \
    && make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    \
    # --- Install executables and data files ---
    # Copy the main executable to a system location on the PATH.
    && cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ \
    # Create the final application directory and copy the required data files into it.
    && mkdir -p /app \
    && cp data/* /app/ \
    \
    # --- Final Cleanup ---
    # Remove build-time dependencies, source code, and package manager caches to reduce final image size.
    && cd / \
    && rm -rf /build \
    && apt-get purge -y --auto-remove git wget cmake build-essential libopenmpi-dev \
    && apt-get autoremove -y \
    && apt-get clean \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set the final working directory for the container.
# This directory contains the necessary input data files for running Laghos.
WORKDIR /app

# Provide a default command to start an interactive shell, allowing the user to execute laghos.
CMD ["/bin/bash"]
```

Hello,

As a debugging agent, I have analyzed the provided Dockerfile and build error. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Identification

The root cause of the build failure is an outdated URL for downloading the METIS library.

The build log clearly shows the following sequence:
1.  `wget` attempts to download from `http://glaros.dtc.umn.edu/gkhome/fetch/sw/metis/metis-5.1.0.tar.gz`.
2.  The server responds with a `301 Moved Permanently` redirect, pointing `wget` to a new location: `https://karypis.github.io/gkhome/fetch/sw/metis/metis-5.1.0.tar.gz`.
3.  `wget` follows the redirect but receives a `404 Not Found` error from the new URL.

This indicates that the METIS source archive is no longer available at the specified location.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this issue, we must update the URL to point to a valid source for METIS and adjust for the new archive's directory structure. The official source code is now hosted on GitHub.

The fix involves two small changes:
1.  Replace the old `wget` URL with the correct one from the official METIS GitHub repository.
2.  Update the `cd` command to match the directory name (`METIS-5.1.0`) created when extracting the archive from GitHub.

# Base Image: Ubuntu 22.04 LTS for a stable, modern environment
FROM ubuntu:22.04

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to prevent prompts during build
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Configure Open MPI for containerized environments, especially on cloud platforms like AWS
# This allows MPI to run as root (common in containers) and correctly uses the container's network interface.
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT=1
ENV OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM=1
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_vader_single_copy_mechanism=none
ENV OMPI_MCA_btl_tcp_if_include=eth0
ENV OMPI_MCA_oob_tcp_if_include=eth0

# A single RUN layer is used to install dependencies, build the application, and clean up.
# This adheres to the constraints of not using multi-stage builds or COPY/ADD commands.
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    g++ \
    gfortran \
    git \
    wget \
    ca-certificates \
    openmpi-bin \
    libopenmpi-dev \
    make \
    cmake \
    && mkdir /build && cd /build \
    \
    # --- Build and install METIS 5.1.0 ---
    # A graph partitioning library required by MFEM.
    && wget http://glaros.dtc.umn.edu/gkhome/fetch/sw/metis/metis-5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && tar -xzvf metis-5.1.0.tar.gz \
    && cd metis-5.1.0 \
    && make config shared=1 prefix=/usr/local \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd .. \
    \
    # --- Build and install Hypre ---
    # A library of high-performance preconditioners and solvers required by MFEM.
    && wget https://github.com/hypre-space/hypre/archive/refs/tags/v2.28.0.tar.gz -O hypre.tar.gz \
    && tar -xzvf hypre.tar.gz \
    && cd hypre-2.28.0/src \
    && ./configure --prefix=/usr/local --disable-fortran --enable-shared \
    && make -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd ../.. \
    \
    # --- Build and install MFEM (Modular Finite Element Methods library) ---
    # The core finite element discretization library on which Laghos is built.
    && git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/mfem/mfem.git \
    && cd mfem \
    && make config MFEM_USE_METIS_5=YES MFEM_USE_MPI=YES HYPRE_DIR=/usr/local METIS_DIR=/usr/local \
    && make parallel -j$(nproc) \
    && make install \
    && cd .. \
    \
    # Update the dynamic linker's cache to find the newly installed shared libraries
    && ldconfig \
    \
    # --- Build Laghos Application ---
    # Clones the latest version from the default branch and builds the executable.
    && git clone --depth 1 --recursive https://github.com/CEED/Laghos.git \
    && cd Laghos \
    && make -j$(nproc) MFEM_DIR=/usr/local \
    \
    # --- Install executables and data files ---
    # Copy the main executable to a system location on the PATH.
    && cp laghos /usr/local/bin/ \
    # Create the final application directory and copy the required data files into it.
    && mkdir -p /app \
    && cp data/* /app/ \
    \
    # --- Final Cleanup ---
    # Remove build-time dependencies, source code, and package manager caches to reduce final image size.
    && cd / \
    && rm -rf /build \
    && apt-get purge -y --auto-remove git wget cmake build-essential libopenmpi-dev \
    && apt-get autoremove -y \
    && apt-get clean \
    && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set the final working directory for the container.
# This directory contains the necessary input data files for running Laghos.
WORKDIR /app

The root cause of the build failure is an outdated URL for downloading the METIS library.

The build log clearly shows the following sequence:
1.  `wget` attempts to download from `http://glaros.dtc.umn.edu/gkhome/fetch/sw/metis/metis-5.1.0.tar.gz`.

The root cause of the build failure is an outdated URL for downloading the METIS library.

1.  `wget` attempts to download from `http://glaros.dtc.umn.edu/gkhome/fetch/sw/metis/metis-5.1.0.tar.gz`.

1.  `wget` attempts to download from `http://glaros.dtc.umn.edu/gkhome/fetch/sw/metis/metis-5.1.0.tar.gz`.

### Error Identification

The root cause of the build failure is an outdated URL for downloading the METIS library.

The build log clearly shows the following sequence:
1.  `wget` attempts to download from `http://glaros.dtc.umn.edu/gkhome/fetch/sw/metis/metis-5.1.0.tar.gz`.

As a debugging expert, I have analyzed the provided Dockerfile and the associated error log. Here is my assessment and the recommended fix.

### Error Identification

The build process is failing during the execution of the main `RUN` command. The error log clearly indicates the problem:

```
20.92 HTTP request sent, awaiting response... 404 Not Found
21.01 2025-09-03 13:23:55 ERROR 404: Not Found.
```

This "404 Not Found" error originates from a `wget` command. The first `wget` in the Dockerfile attempts to download the METIS library from a GitHub archive URL. This URL is proving to be unreliable or is incorrect, causing the download to fail and terminating the build.

### Recommended Fix

The solution is to replace the unstable GitHub URL for METIS with the official, stable download link from the METIS project's website. This also requires updating the name of the directory that is entered after the archive is extracted, as the official tarball creates a directory with a different name (`metis-5.1.0`) than the GitHub archive (`METIS-v5.1.0`).

I have corrected the `wget` and `cd` commands for the METIS installation accordingly.

### Error Identification

The root cause of the build failure is an outdated URL for downloading the METIS library.

The build log clearly shows the following sequence:
1.  `wget` attempts to download from `http://glaros.dtc.umn.edu/gkhome/fetch/sw/metis/metis-5.1.0.tar.gz`.
2.  The server responds with a `301 Moved Permanently` redirect, pointing `wget` to a new location: `https://karypis.github.io/gkhome/fetch/sw/metis/metis-5.1.0.tar.gz`.
3.  `wget` follows the redirect but receives a `404 Not Found` error from the new URL.

This indicates that the METIS source archive is no longer available at the specified location.

### Recommended Fix

To resolve this issue, we must update the URL to point to a valid source for METIS and adjust for the new archive's directory structure. The official source code is now hosted on GitHub.

The fix involves two small changes:
1.  Replace the old `wget` URL with the correct one from the official METIS GitHub repository.
2.  Update the `cd` command to match the directory name (`METIS-5.1.0`) created when extracting the archive from GitHub.
